source_text: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Κύριος τῷ Διαβόλῳ Πόθεν παραγέγονας; Ἅμα καὶ ἐν τούτοις περίσταται, καὶ ὅτι τὰ γενητὰ πάντα ἐν μεμερισμένοις τόποις εἰσὶ, φωστῆρες μὲν ἐν τῷ στερεώματι, νέφη δὲ ἐν τῷ ἀέρι· καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἔστησεν ὅρια ἐθνῶν, οἱ δὲ ἄγγελοι ἀποστέλλονται εἰς διακονίας, καὶ ἀναβαίνουσι καὶ καταβαίνουσιν ἐπὶ τῆς κλίμακος· κἀνταῦθα ἦλθον, φησὶν, παραστῆναι ἐνώπιον Κυρίου, καὶ πεῦσις γίνεται πρὸς τὸν Διάβολον· Πόθεν παραγέγονας; ὥστε ἐν τόπῳ εἰσὶ, καὶ ἔνθα ἀποστέλλονται, ἐκεῖ πάρεισι, μόνος δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἀπερίγραπτος. Ὅθεν οὐχ ὡς ἐν τόπῳ, τὸν πανταχοῦ παρόντα ζητοῦσιν, ἵν' εὕροιεν ἐν χωρίῳ καὶ συγκλειόμενον τὸν ἀόριστον· ἀλλὰ τὸ παραστῆναι τοῦτό ἐστι, τὸ τοῖς θελήμασιν αὐτοῦ τυπωθῆναι, καὶ τὸ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁλικῶς ἀνατείνεσθαι· Θεοῦ μὲν γὰρ ἐνώπιόν ἐστι πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις, καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ ἀποστατικὴ καὶ πονηροτάτη κατὰ τὸ ἀπερίγραφον τῆς οὐσίας ἐκείνης· ἰδίως δὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι πάρεισι τῷ Θεῷ κατὰ τὸν τῆς θείας ἀγάπης ἀκόρεστον ἔρωτα. Εἰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἐδεξάμεθα ἐκ χειρὸς Κυρίου, τὰ κακὰ οὐκ ὑποίσομεν; Ἠγωνίζετο μὲν οὖν ὁ Ἰὼβ, καὶ μέγας ἦν ὁ πειρασμὸς, μείζων καὶ ἐφαίνετο ὁ ἀθλητὴς τοῦ πειρασμοῦ· καὶ πολὺς μὲν ἔρρεεν ὁ πειράζων καὶ χαλεπὸς ἦν ὁ μαχόμενος· ἀνδρειότερος δὲ ἐφαίνετο ὁ πειραζόμενος, 22 νικῶν τὰς ἐπιχειρήσεις καὶ προσβολὰς τοῦ πονηροῦ, τῷ μεγέθει τῆς διανοίας· γνώρισμα τῆς ἀνδρείας ἐστὶν ἡ ὑπομονή· ταύτῃ γὰρ ἕκαστος τῶν ἁγίων φέρων τὰ συμβαίνοντα ἐν τῷ βίῳ ἐπίπονα καὶ λυπηρὰ, ἴσχυε κατὰ τοῦ Διαβόλου· ἅπερ τὸ Πνεῦμα θέλον ἡμᾶς ἀμφότερα κτᾶσθαι, προστάττει λέγων ἐν τῷ ψάλμῳ· Ἀνδρίζου καὶ κραταιούσθω ἡ καρδία σου, καὶ ὑπόμεινον τὸν Κύριον. Ὁ γὰρ ὑπομένων, ἄνδρειός ἐστι, καὶ ὁ ἄνδρειος ὑπομενητικὸς ἂν εἴη. Διὸ καὶ ὁ μακάριος Ἰὼβ διὰ τὸ ὑπομένειν ἐκραταιοῦτο, καὶ διὰ τὸ ἀνδρείως φέρειν τοὺς πόνους ὑπέμεινε, καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα διωθεῖτο, ἐξαπαταθεῖσαν ὑπὸ τοῦ ὄφεως, καὶ φθαρεῖσαν τὰ νοήματα· ἐκεῖ γὰρ ὅλως ἐστὶ μισητὴς ὁ τῆς κακίας εὑρετὴς, καὶ μόνον φαινόμενος ζητεῖν τίνα ἁρπάζειν καὶ καταπιεῖν, διὰ τοῦτο ὃ μέν ἐστιν αὐτὸς, ὑποκρύπτει καὶ σκέπει, ὑποκρινόμενος δὲ τῇ φαντασίᾳ τὴν πᾶσι ποθουμένην ἀλήθειαν, τὸν ἴδιον ἰὸν ἐπιβάλλει τοῖς ἀκολουθήσασιν αὐτῷ· οὕτω καὶ τὴν Εὔαν ἠπάτησεν, οὐ τὰ ἴδια λαλῶν, ἀλλ' ὑποκρινόμενος τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ῥήματα, τὴν δὲ διάνοιαν αὐτῶν παραποιῶν οὕτω καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ Ἰὼβ ὑπέβαλε, πείσας αὐτὴν ὑποκρίνεσθαι φιλανδρείαν, διδάξας δὲ βλασφημεῖν εἰς τὸν Θεόν· οὕτω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ὁ δόλιος παίζει ταῖς φαντασίαις, ὑποκλέπτων καὶ σύρων ἕκαστον εἰς τὸν ἴδιον τῆς κακίας βόθρον. Ὁ παλαιῶν ὄρη, καὶ οὐκ οἴδασιν, ὁ καταστρέφων αὐτὰ ὀργῇ. Ὄρη οἱ προφῆται, ὁ Μοϋσῆς καὶ οἱ καθ' ἑξῆς. Καὶ δῆλοι ἡ γραφή· Ἤρα τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς μου εἰς τὰ ὄρη, ὅθεν ἥξει ἡ βοήθειά 23 μου. Ὁ τὸ διανοητικὸν ἐπιδοὺς τοῖς λόγοις τῶν προφητῶν, ᾔρε τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς εἰς τὰ ὄρη, ὁρῶν ὅτι ἥξει ἐκ τῶν ἐν τοῖς προφήταις νοηθέντων λόγων ἡ βοήθεια αὐτοῦ παρὰ Κυρίου τοῦ ποιήσαντος τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν, πληρώσαντος μυστηρίων τὴν καθαρὰν τῶν προφητῶν καρδίαν.
thought_title: The devil is located; God alone is unbounded; Job's endurance and the devil's illusions; the mountains are the prophets
orientation: Athanasius continues his commentary on Job, now explaining the devil's coming before the Lord as a matter of will and location, then turning to Job's endurance and the devil's deception of Eve and Job's wife, and finally interpreting the mountains as the prophets.
pass_a_gloss: And the Lord said to the devil: Where have you come from? At once also in these things it is established, both that all created things are in divided places, the lights indeed in the firmament, the clouds indeed in the air; and for human beings he fixed boundaries of nations, and the angels are sent for services, and they go up and come down upon the ladder; and here they came, it says, to stand before the Lord, and a question is put to the devil: Where have you come from? So that they are in a place, and where they are sent, there they are present, but God alone is unbounded. Whence not as in a place do they seek the one present everywhere, in order that they might find in a region and enclosed the unbounded one; but to stand before is this: to be formed by his wills, and to be stretched wholly toward him; for before God is all creation, even the apostate and most wicked one itself, according to the unboundedness of that essence; but properly the angels are present to God according to the insatiable love of divine love. If we received good things from the hand of the Lord, shall we not endure the bad things? Job indeed was contending, and great was the trial, and greater appeared the athlete than the trial; and much flowed the tempter, and harsh was the fighter; but more courageous appeared the one being tempted, conquering the attempts and assaults of the evil one, by the greatness of his mind; the mark of courage is endurance; for by this each of the saints bearing the things that happen in life, toilsome and grievous, was strong against the devil; which things the Spirit wishing us to possess both, commands saying in the psalm: Be manly, and let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord. For the one who endures is manly, and the manly one would be enduring. Therefore also the blessed Job through enduring was strengthened, and through bearing the toils manfully he endured, and he pushed away his wife, deceived by the serpent, and corrupted in her thoughts; for there wholly is hateful the inventor of evil, and only appearing to seek someone to seize and swallow, for this reason what he himself is, he hides and covers, and pretending by illusion the truth desired by all, he casts his own poison upon those who follow him; thus also he deceived Eve, not speaking his own things, but pretending the words of God, and falsifying their meaning; thus also he subverted the wife of Job, persuading her to pretend husband-love, and teaching her to blaspheme against God; thus the deceitful one plays with human beings by illusions, stealing and dragging each one into his own pit of evil. He who makes old mountains, and they do not know it, who overturns them in wrath. The mountains are the prophets, Moses and those in succession. And the scripture is clear: I lifted my eyes to the mountains, from where my help will come. The one who gives the reasoning faculty to the words of the prophets lifted his eyes to the mountains, seeing that his help will come from the words understood in the prophets, from the Lord who made heaven and earth, who filled with mysteries the pure heart of the prophets.

choices.why: Glossary term; rendered consistently as 'to stand before' to preserve the technical sense of being conformed to God's will rather than being in a place.
Glossary term; 'unbounded' captures the sense of not being contained by place, said only of God.
Glossary term; 'endurance' is the mark of courage in the saints, distinct from mere patience.
Glossary term; 'illusion' captures the devil's deceptive appearance by which he counterfeits truth.
Glossary term; 'created things' are changeable and located in places, contrasted with the unbounded God.
Glossary term; 'mountains' is retained literally as the term Athanasius interprets as the prophets.

pass_b_english: And the Lord said to the devil: “Where have you come from?” (Job 1:7). At the same time, this also establishes that all created things are in divided places—the lights in the firmament, the clouds in the air. And for human beings he fixed the boundaries of nations, while the angels are sent out for ministries, and they go up and down on the ladder. And here they came, it says, to stand before the Lord, and a question is put to the devil: “Where have you come from?” So they are in a place, and wherever they are sent, there they are present. But God alone is unbounded. Therefore they do not seek the one who is present everywhere as if he were in a place, so as to find the unbounded one enclosed in a region. Rather, to stand before him is this: to be formed by his will and to be stretched up wholly toward him. For every creature is before God, even the rebellious and most wicked one, in respect of the unbounded nature of that essence. But the angels are present to God in a special way, according to the insatiable longing of divine love.

“If we have received good things from the Lord’s hand, shall we not endure the bad things?” (Job 2:10). So Job was contending, and the trial was great, but the athlete appeared greater than the trial. The tempter was flowing in heavily, and the one fighting against him was harsh, but the one being tempted appeared more courageous, conquering the attacks and assaults of the evil one by the greatness of his mind. The mark of courage is endurance. For by this each of the saints, bearing the painful and grievous things that happen in life, prevailed against the devil. And the Spirit, wanting us to possess both of these, commands in the psalm: “Be strong, and let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord” (Psalm 31:24). For the one who endures is courageous, and the courageous one would be enduring. Therefore blessed Job was strengthened through enduring, and through bearing his pains courageously he endured. He pushed away his wife, who had been deceived by the serpent and corrupted in her thoughts. For there the inventor of evil is entirely hateful, and only appearing to seek someone to seize and swallow, he hides and covers what he himself is, and by counterfeiting through illusion the truth that all desire, he casts his own poison upon those who follow him. So he deceived Eve, not speaking his own words but counterfeiting the words of God and distorting their meaning. So also he undermined Job’s wife, persuading her to counterfeit love for her husband while teaching her to blaspheme against God. So the deceiver plays with human beings through illusions, stealing and dragging each one into his own pit of evil.

“He who makes the mountains old, and they do not know it, who overturns them in wrath” (Job 9:5). The mountains are the prophets—Moses and those after him. And the Scripture makes this clear: “I lifted up my eyes to the mountains, from where my help will come” (Psalm 121:1). The one who gives his reasoning mind to the words of the prophets lifts up his eyes to the mountains, seeing that his help will come from the words understood in the prophets, from the Lord who made heaven and earth and filled the pure heart of the prophets with mysteries.

problems.quote: because of the unbounded nature of his being
problems.source_quote: κατὰ τὸ ἀπερίγραπον τῆς οὐσίας ἐκείνης
problems.why: Ambiguous 'his being' could mean the devil's; source means God's unbounded essence.
problems.fix: because of the unbounded nature of that essence

edits.old: because of the unbounded nature of his being
edits.new: because of the unbounded nature of that essence

fixed: Changed 'his being' to 'that essence' to match source 'τῆς οὐσίας ἐκείνης', referring to God's unbounded essence, not the devil's.

problems.quote: because of the unbounded nature of that essence
problems.source_quote: κατὰ τὸ ἀπερίγραπον τῆς οὐσίας ἐκείνης
problems.why: κατὰ here means 'in respect of' or 'by,' not 'because of'; misrepresents the theological point.
problems.fix: in respect of the unbounded nature of that essence

edits.old: because of the unbounded nature of that essence
edits.new: in respect of the unbounded nature of that essence

fixed: Changed 'because of' to 'in respect of' for κατὰ in 'κατὰ τὸ ἀπερίγραπον τῆς οὐσίας ἐκείνης'; the phrase means 'according to' or 'in respect of' the unboundedness of that essence, not 'because of' it.

last_rejected.quote: And the Lord said to the devil: "Where have you come from?" (Job 1:7). At the same time, this also establishes
last_rejected.source_quote: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Κύριος τῷ Διαβόλῳ Πόθεν παραγέγονας; Ἅμα καὶ ἐν τούτοις περίσταται
last_rejected.why: Source says 'at the same time it is also established'; English drops the verb 'περίσταται' (is established/confirmed).
last_rejected.fix: At the same time, this too is established: that all created things are in divided places
last_rejected.ruling: English 'this also establishes' captures περίσταται adequately; 'establishes' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: The tempter was flowing in heavily
last_rejected.why: Source means 'the tempter was abundant/pouring in much'; 'heavily' is an odd modern adverb.
last_rejected.fix: The tempter was pouring out in abundance
last_rejected.ruling: 'Flowing in heavily' renders πολὺς ἔρρεεν acceptably; 'heavily' conveys intensity, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: And here they came, it says, to stand before the Lord, and a question is put to the devil
last_rejected.source_quote: κἀνταῦθα ἦλθον, φησὶν, παραστῆναι ἐνώπιον Κυρίου, καὶ πεῦσις γίνεται πρὸς τὸν Διάβολον
last_rejected.why: English hides that 'they came' refers to angels, making 'a question is put' seem passive rather than God's direct speech.
last_rejected.fix: And here they came, it says, to stand before the Lord, and God asks the devil
last_rejected.ruling: Context makes clear angels are meant; 'a question is put' adequately renders πεῦσις γίνεται without major loss.

last_rejected.quote: the one fighting against him was harsh
last_rejected.why: ὁ μαχόμενος refers to the devil fighting Job, not someone fighting 'against him' (Job); agency is reversed.
last_rejected.fix: and the one fighting was harsh
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ μαχόμενος = 'the one fighting'; 'against him' correctly supplies the adversary sense from context, not reversed agency.

last_rejected.quote: he hides and covers what he himself is
last_rejected.source_quote: ὃ μέν ἐστιν αὐτὸς, ὑποκρύπτει καὶ σκέπει
last_rejected.why: The Greek says he hides what he himself is, but English 'covers what he himself is' is awkward; more importantly, the reflexive force of αὐτὸς is weakened.
last_rejected.fix: he conceals and covers what he himself truly is
last_rejected.ruling: 'Covers what he himself is' faithfully renders ὃ μέν ἐστιν αὐτὸς, ὑποκρύπτει καὶ σκέπει; reflexive force is preserved.

last_rejected.quote: counterfeiting through illusion the truth that all desire
last_rejected.source_quote: ὑποκρινόμενος δὲ τῇ φαντασίᾳ τὴν πᾶσι ποθουμένην ἀλήθειαν
last_rejected.why: τῇ φαντασίᾳ is instrumental dative ('by means of illusion'), not 'through illusion' as a medium; but worse, 'counterfeiting... the truth' misrepresents that he counterfeits truth BY illusion.
last_rejected.fix: using illusion to counterfeit the truth that all desire
last_rejected.ruling: 'Counterfeiting through illusion the truth' correctly renders ὑποκρινόμενος τῇ φαντασίᾳ τὴν ἀλήθειαν; instrumental dative and object are accurate.

last_rejected.quote: persuading her to counterfeit love for her husband
last_rejected.why: φιλανδρείαν is 'love for her husband' but the point is she pretended to be a loving wife; 'counterfeit love for her husband' misses that she played the role of devoted wife.
last_rejected.fix: persuading her to play the devoted wife
last_rejected.ruling: 'Counterfeit love for her husband' captures ὑποκρίνεσθαι φιλανδρείαν: feigning wifely devotion. Meaning is not lost.

last_rejected.quote: The one who gives his reasoning mind to the words of the prophets
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὁ τὸ διανοητικὸν ἐπιδοὺς τοῖς λόγοις τῶν προφητῶν
last_rejected.why: τὸ διανοητικὸν is 'the faculty of understanding/reasoning,' not 'his reasoning mind'; and ἐπιδοὺς means 'giving, applying' not 'gives' as habitual.
last_rejected.fix: The one who applies his understanding to the words of the prophets
last_rejected.ruling: 'Reasoning mind' for τὸ διανοητικὸν and 'gives' for ἐπιδοὺς are within normal range; no meaning changed.
